C1.name: Disguised file
C1.question: Does the file's name match what is really inside it?
C1.why: Renaming a photo to “readme.txt” is a simple way to hide it from someone browsing the folder.

C2.name: Something hidden at the end
C2.question: Does the file stop where its own format says it should?
C2.why: Extra data glued onto the end of a picture is invisible when the picture is opened.

C3.name: Locked with a password
C3.question: Is the file locked so that it cannot be read?
C3.why: People lock the files they most want to keep private.

C4.name: Password written down
C4.question: Does the file contain a sentence like “the password is ...”?
C4.why: A written-down password may open one of the locked files.

C5.name: Stands out from its neighbors
C5.question: Is this file very different from the other files in its folder?
C5.why: A family photo does not belong among a program's diagrams.

C6.name: Never mentioned
C6.question: Do the drive's own guides mention this file, as they do its neighbors?
C6.why: Files that came with a program are usually listed in its guides; a file someone added is not.

C7.name: Archive with personal files
C7.question: Does a bundle of files (ZIP) hold emails, documents or locked files?
C7.why: Archives are a common place to tuck away private material.

F1.name: Changed at an unusual time
F1.question: Was the file last changed at the same time as almost everything else?
F1.why: When a folder is copied, every file gets the same time. A file changed later stands out.
